title: Pork shish kabob with vegetables, excluding potatoes

content.title: About
content.content: Pork shish kabob with vegetables, excluding potatoes is made from bite‑size pieces of tender pork marinated in spices and fresh vegetables (bell pepper, onion, zucchini, tomato). The ingredients are skewered and grilled over open flame or on a grill until a golden crust forms, keeping the meat juicy and the vegetables flavorful.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shish kebab originates from the nomadic peoples of the Caucasus and Central Asia.
Pork cooks quickly on the grill because the small cubes and the acidic marinade tenderize the meat.
Adding vegetables boosts the content of vitamins C and A and gives the dish a vivid colour.
Excluding potatoes reduces the starch load, making the dish more suitable for low‑carb diets.
Kebabs are often served with a yogurt‑herb‑lemon sauce.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Pork provides high‑quality complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pork contains vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for immunity and bone health.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Bell peppers and tomatoes are rich in vitamin C and lycopene, antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Without potatoes the meal has a lower carb count, helping to maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Charring
items.content: Over‑charred meat can form carcinogenic compounds; grill to a golden brown, not blackened, crust.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an intolerance or allergy to pork.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Marinades often contain salt; people with hypertension should monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Ensure the pork is cooked through to avoid salmonella or other bacterial risks.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the kebab hot, removing the meat and vegetables from the skewers. Eat directly from the skewer, cut into bite‑size pieces for salads or wraps, or pair with a light yogurt‑based sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked kebab can be kept in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Reheat until the internal temperature reaches 71 °C.
